title: Back up your recovery phrase
summary: Write down the 24 words that bring your HumanityOS account back on any device, and keep them where only you can find them.
for: Anyone with an account in the HumanityOS desktop app. Do it right after you make your account, before you close the app, and again if you ever lose the paper.

tools.note: Paper you will keep: a page of a notebook, or a card.

steps.text: Find a private moment: nobody watching, and nothing streaming, recording or sharing your screen.
why: Whoever sees the words can use your account. The app covers them until you choose to show them for this reason, and covers them again when you switch to another window.

steps.text: Under Account & Recovery Phrase, beside Reveal recovery phrase, type your passphrase and press Unlock.
detail: If you made this identity a moment ago and have not set a passphrase yet, the words are already there, still covered. Until you set a passphrase, a new identity is kept only while the app is open: write the words down before you close it.
If the protected setup is on (Settings, Safety), press Show the recovery phrase and enter its PIN; then the passphrase is asked as above.

steps.text: Press and hold Hold to show the words until they appear.
why: The hold, three seconds, is so that a stray click never shows them.

steps.text: Write all 24 words on the paper in order, with the number of each beside it.
detail: Write them by hand rather than pressing Copy beside them: copied words stay on the computer's clipboard, where other programs can read them (our reading).

steps.text: Read each word on the paper against the screen. Do all 24 match, in the same order?
Press Hide the words, then Lock if it is there.
Keep the paper somewhere safe and private where you will find it again.

safety.short: Anyone who has these words can use your account. Nobody from HumanityOS or any server will ever ask for them. Type them only into this app, to restore your account (Restore from Recovery Phrase, or Restore an existing account from its recovery phrase when the app first opens) or to reset the protected setup's PIN (Forgot the PIN?), and never send them.
full: The recovery phrase backs up your account and your wallet. When the app makes a new identity it says so plainly: these words are the only way to recover the account.

Do not photograph them, or keep them in email, a notes app or cloud storage (our reading: photos and notes are easily copied to a cloud account without your noticing, and email and cloud storage are kept on other people's computers).

steps.text: If you want a second way back in, Settings, Account also has Recovery through trusted people.
detail: You choose a few friends; each keeps one piece of your recovery phrase, locked, and enough of them together can help you back in if you lose your device and the paper too. The paper is still the main way back.

worked_if: The 24 words are on paper, checked against the screen, in order.
The words are covered again and the paper is somewhere private.

problems.sign: There is no Reveal recovery phrase, only Generate New Identity.
problems.why: This device has no identity yet.
problems.fix: If you have used HumanityOS before, restore yours with Restore from Recovery Phrase, below it, rather than generating one: a new identity is a different account. Otherwise generate one; its words are shown covered, ready to write down.

problems.sign: It says your identity is on this device, locked.
problems.why: The app opens with your identity locked unless you chose Remember on this device.
problems.fix: That is how it opens: type your passphrase beside Reveal recovery phrase and press Unlock, as in the unlock step. It unlocks your identity and shows the words, covered.

problems.why: The passphrase is the one that locks this identity on this device.
problems.fix: Type it again: press Show beside the box to see what you typed.

problems.sign: You do not remember the passphrase.
problems.why: The app may open without it (Remember on this device, or a Quick PIN), but showing the words always asks for it.
problems.fix: The words cannot be shown without it. While the app is open, set up Recovery through trusted people (Settings, Account), so a lost device is not the end of the account.

problems.sign: Someone may have seen the words, or a copy of them left the paper.
problems.why: Whoever has the words can use your account, from any device.
problems.fix: Under Replace Identity in Settings, Account, press Generate New Identity (replace current), then Yes, generate a new identity. When it asks for a passphrase, set one and press Encrypt Key: until you do, the new identity is kept only while the app is open. Then back up the new words. The old words still open the old identity, so whoever has them can still act as it: let the people you know find you under the new one. They also open the old wallet: if it holds anything, move it to the new identity's wallet straight away (our reading).

problems.sign: You pressed Copy beside the words.
problems.why: The words are now on the computer's clipboard, where other programs can read them (our reading).
problems.fix: Copy something else to replace them. If clipboard history is on (Windows key + V on Windows), delete the entry there too. If you pasted them anywhere, or your clipboard is shared with your other devices, treat it as Someone may have seen the words (our reading).

sources.title: Settings, Account: Account & Recovery Phrase
sources.quote: Anyone who has it can use your account, so never share it.
sources.note: The desktop app's own code, as it stood on 2026-10-23 (commit 1638661e8): the section's words, the passphrase gate titled Reveal recovery phrase, the protected setup's PIN, the 24 words and Generate New Identity. Re-read 2026-10-24 with BUG-213's fix: an identity that is on the device but locked shows the same Reveal recovery phrase gate, which also unlocks it, and never Generate New Identity; Restore says it replaces the identity on the device; Replace Identity asks Yes, generate a new identity, then for a passphrase. The website's Settings words differ, so this how-to is for the desktop app.

sources.title: The recovery phrase cover
sources.quote: Only show these when nobody can see your screen: not while streaming, recording or sharing your screen, and not where people can look over your shoulder.
sources.note: Hold to show the words (a 3 second hold), Hide the words, and the words covering themselves when the window is not the one in front. As the code stood on 2026-10-23.

sources.title: lockable_gate: Show, Unlock and the passphrase box
sources.note: The Show and Hide button beside the passphrase box, Unlock, Lock, and the words Wrong passphrase. As the code stood on 2026-10-23.

sources.title: Settings, Account: Recovery through trusted people
sources.note: Friends each keep one piece of the recovery phrase, locked; the recovery phrase stays the main way back in. Setting it up uses the identity unlocked in the app, without asking for the passphrase again. As the code stood on 2026-10-23; re-read 2026-10-24.

sources.title: The passphrase prompt: Encrypt Your Private Key, Unlock Private Key
sources.note: After Generate New Identity the prompt asks for a passphrase to encrypt the new key; skipping it leaves the key in memory only. The app opens with the identity locked, without asking, unless Remember on this device was chosen; the unlock prompt opens from Unlock Key (Settings, Security) or the chat's Unlock with Passphrase, can be skipped (limited mode), and can remember the key in the OS keychain. As the code stood on 2026-10-24.

sources.title: AppConfig::from_gui_state: what the app saves
sources.quote: Never write plaintext key back; use encrypted fields from state
sources.note: The saved settings hold the key only encrypted with the passphrase, so a key that was never encrypted is not saved. As the code stood on 2026-10-24.

sources.title: The protected setup's words
sources.note: Forgot the PIN? resets the PIN with the recovery phrase. While the protected setup is on, showing the recovery phrase needs the PIN; the desktop's button asks for it (src/gui/pages/safety_protected.rs), and the passphrase gate follows. As the data stood on 2026-10-24.

sources.title: The first-run screen
sources.quote: Restore an existing account from its recovery phrase
sources.note: The first-run screen's way back in with the recovery phrase. As the code stood on 2026-10-24.

sources.title: Safety warnings: Asking for your recovery phrase or keys
sources.quote: Nobody from HumanityOS or any server will ever ask for your recovery phrase. Never type it into a message.
sources.note: The warning the chat shows when a message asks for the recovery phrase. As the data stood on 2026-10-24.

sources.title: The recovery phrase guard on sending
sources.quote: Nobody legitimate will ever ask for it.
sources.note: What the chat says when it stops a message holding the recovery phrase; there is no send anyway. As the code stood on 2026-10-24.
